title: EF-IMR: Embedded Flash with Interlaced Magnetic Recording Technology
problem: Interlaced Magnetic Recording (IMR) increases storage density via track overlap but introduces severe latency from Read-Modify-Write (RMW) operations that affect underlying tracks, requiring costly head repositioning.
motivation: Storage density improvements via IMR must be balanced with performance; RMW latency and head movement overhead negate density gains.
method: When data is written to overlapping magnetic disk tracks, it can disturb neighbors, requiring expensive read-modify-write fix-ups to keep data correct. EF-IMR minimizes these fix-ups through smart scheduling (reducing disk head movement), write merging (combining multiple writes), and skip detection (avoiding unnecessary operations).
key_novelty: EF-IMR maintains data safety during crashes on overlapping-track magnetic disks while reducing wasted disk head movement by intelligently scheduling which fix-up operations to perform and skipping those that aren't needed.
contributions: Crash consistency guarantees under intensive I/O workloads
Maintains IMR density benefits while reducing performance penalty

metrics.other: 20.11% RMW latency reduction, 89.37% head movement reduction

limitations: Evaluation limited to specific I/O patterns; applicability to SSD/NVMe or multi-head systems not discussed.
primary_theme: crash-consistent IMR storage with RMW overhead reduction
